::: {.lead}
My research asks how the geometry of string compactifications encodes the microscopic
physics of quantum gravity. I focus on asymptotic regions of moduli space, where towers
of states become light, effective strings can emerge, and quantum corrections can
invalidate the classical effective description.
:::

::: {.plain-language-box}
### The basic idea

Compactification geometry determines physical quantities such as particle masses,
couplings, and field-space distances. Near singular boundaries, these quantities obey
universal asymptotic patterns. By understanding the geometry of those patterns, one can
identify the new degrees of freedom that appear and test whether the low-energy theory
remains consistent.
:::

## Research programme

:::: {.research-grid}

::: {.research-card}
### Infinite-distance limits and emergent strings {#infinite-distance}

**Question.** What microscopic degrees of freedom become light when a scalar field
travels an infinite distance in moduli space?

**Approach.** I combine Hodge-theoretic degeneration data with the geometry of
Calabi–Yau fibrations and vanishing cycles. This makes it possible to identify BPS
particles, effective strings, Kaluza–Klein towers, and the appropriate higher-dimensional
duality frame.

**Why it matters.** The analysis provides a concrete realisation of the idea that
infinite-distance limits are controlled by emergent weakly coupled descriptions rather
than by an arbitrary breakdown of effective field theory.

**Related work:** [Emergent strings](https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP01(2026)140) ·
[Physics and geometry of complex-structure limits](https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP03(2026)063)
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Asymptotic Hodge theory {#hodge-theory}

**Question.** How can one extract reliable physics when exact Calabi–Yau periods are
unknown or computationally inaccessible?

**Approach.** Nilpotent-orbit and $SL(2)$-orbit techniques provide universal control near
singular boundaries. I develop these mathematical structures into calculational tools
for moduli-space metrics, gauge couplings, flux potentials, BPS masses, and
multi-parameter limits.

**Why it matters.** This replaces model-by-model calculations with structural methods
that apply across large classes of compactifications.

**Related work:** [Finiteness and flux counting](https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP08(2024)039) ·
[Bi-Yang–Baxter models and $SL(2)$-orbits](https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP11(2023)123)
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Quantum obstructions in $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories {#quantum-obstructions}

**Question.** Does a classical infinite-distance limit remain meaningful after quantum
effects are included?

**Approach.** I study how complex-structure limits backreact on the string-coupling and
Kähler sectors in Type IIB/F-theory compactifications. Worldsheet consistency,
instanton corrections, and the geometry of elliptic Calabi–Yau fourfolds provide
complementary diagnostics.

**Why it matters.** A trajectory that looks consistent in a factorised classical action
can fail in the genuine quantum theory, with consequences for asymptotic control and
string model building.

**Related work:** [Part I: $g_s$ obstructions](https://doi.org/10.1103/blb9-hrwd) ·
[Part II: Kähler obstructions](https://doi.org/10.1103/ypyx-mg6r)
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Finiteness and the flux landscape {#finiteness}

**Question.** When are families of flux vacua finite, and how complicated can their
distribution become near singular regions of moduli space?

**Approach.** I combine asymptotic Hodge theory with tools from tame and o-minimal
geometry to formulate precise finiteness statements and counting conjectures.

**Why it matters.** Finiteness questions connect the local geometry of compactification
spaces to the global structure and predictivity of the string landscape.

**Related work:** [Finiteness theorems and counting conjectures](https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP08(2024)039)
:::

::::

## Methodological perspective

My work operates across four mutually reinforcing levels:

- **Effective field theory:** field-space metrics, BPS objects, towers of states,
  quantum corrections, and duality frames.
- **Calabi–Yau geometry:** degenerations, fibrations, singularities, vanishing cycles,
  and special Lagrangian geometry.
- **Hodge theory:** period maps, limiting mixed Hodge structures, nilpotent orbits,
  and asymptotic $SL(2)$ data.
- **Quantum-gravity constraints:** distance, emergence, finiteness, and the limits of
  perturbative control.

::: {.info-box}
The unifying objective is not only to classify asymptotic behaviours, but to identify
their microscopic physics and determine which apparently consistent classical limits
survive in the full quantum theory.
:::
